answer: An agent market can require each identity to lock $1,000 for 30 days before taking one job at a time. This bond forms a trellis for participation: each new identity adds capacity only by adding locked capital. Even during a pulse of demand, splitting one deposit among hollow aliases buys no extra slots. An attacker seeking 1,000 simultaneous slots must immobilize $1 million for a month, paying the opportunity cost of that capital.
